judge_response:
ANALYSIS: A rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus (FDP) tendon at its insertion into the distal phalanx results in an inability to flex the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint — this is the definition of *jersey finger*, not mallet finger. In contrast, *mallet finger* is caused by rupture or avulsion of the *extensor digitorum communis* (EDC) tendon from the dorsal base of the distal phalanx, leading to inability to actively extend the DIP joint (i.e., persistent DIP flexion). The two conditions involve opposite muscle groups (flexor vs. extensor), opposite joint motion deficits (loss of flexion vs. loss of extension), and distinct mechanisms/injuries. The prediction incorrectly conflates them.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
